**Alvorlig blødning** (severe bleeding) is a critical clinical condition and the primary outcome variable for Indicator 7 in the evaluation of atrial fibrillation treatment quality in Denmark [^src1]. It serves as a central quality parameter that directly influences treatment decisions and political guidelines regarding the safety of anticoagulation therapy [^src1]. 

The condition is specifically defined as intracranial, gastrointestinal, urinary tract, or pulmonary bleeding identified via the National Patient Register [^src1]. To standardize this definition, the criteria provided by the [[international-society-of-thrombosis-and-hemostasis|International Society of Thrombosis and Hemostasis]] (ISTH) are adapted for use in this context [^src2]. The definition explicitly includes subtypes such as [[intrakraniel-bloedning|Intrakraniel blødning]] and [[iskaemisk-apopleksi|Iskæmisk apopleksi]] [^src1].

Epidemiological data from the report highlights the incidence of severe bleeding among [[praevalente-patienter-med-atrieflimren|Prævalente patienter med atrieflimren]] (prevalent patients with atrial fibrillation). Overall, 2.2% of these prevalent patients were admitted with severe bleeding during the reporting period, with regional variations ranging from 1.9% to 2.2% across the [[regionernes-kliniske-kvalitetsudviklingsprogram|Regionernes Kliniske Kvalitetsudviklingsprogram]] [^src1]. For incident patients, the national rate of severe bleeding one year after diagnosis was 3.2%, varying regionally from 2.8% to 3.8% [^src1]. 

A significant clinical challenge highlighted by the data is that 43.7% of severe bleedings occurred among patients with a low [[cha2ds2-vasc|CHA2DS2-VASc]] score of 0 or 1 [^src1]. Furthermore, pharmacovigilance data indicates that the proportion of patients experiencing severe bleeding was 2.30% for those treated with [[doac|DOAC]] and 2.38% for those treated with [[marevan|marevan]] [^src1].
